REBUTTAL TESTIMONY OF AMY G. THOMASON ON BEHALF OF SWG BRIGGS I,

REBUTTAL TESTIMONY oF AMY G. THOMASON                                                           2
                                    I.      INTRODUCTION

Q.    Please state your name and address.

A.    My name is Dr. Amy G. Thomason. My address is 8404 Bear Creek Drive, Austin, Texas
      78737.
Q.    Please state your background.

A.    I am a licensed veterinarian in the State of Texas and have been licensed since 2007.

Q.    Are you the same Amy G. Thomason that provided direct testimony in this docket on
      behalf of SWG Briggs I, L.P.?

A.    Yes, I am.

Q.    What testimony will you be addressing in your rebuttal testimony?

A.    I will be addressing testimony filed by or on behalf ofApplicants Oncor Electric Delivery
      Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation, including testimony from
      Russel J. Marusak and Kevin Wells regarding routing, environmental review, prudent
      avoidance, and compliance with Commission routing requirements.

Q.    Was this material prepared by you or under your supervision and guidance?

A.    Yes.

Q.    Is the information contained in your rebuttal testimony and exhibits true and correct
      to the best of your knowledge and belief?

A.    Yes.

                      II.    REBUTTAL TO MARUSAK TESTIMONY

Q.    Have you reviewed the testimony of Russell J. Marusak?

A.    Yes.

Q.    Do you agree with Mr. Marusak's conclusion that the proposed transmission line
      routes, including Link G9, should not have significant impacts on land use,
      environmental resources, wildlife habitat, or agricultural operations?

A.    No. I strongly disagree with that conclusion as it applies to the Properties owned by SWG
      Briggs I, L.P. and the surrounding rural community. In my opinion, the proposed Link G9
      route would create substantial and permanent impacts to active agricultural operations,




REBUTTAL TESTIMONY oF AMY G. THOMASON                                                         3
       wildlife habitat, rural land use, aesthetics, future residential use, groundwater planning, and
      the Northeast Burnet County Water District 1.

Q.    Why do you believe Mr. Marusak's conclusions are insufficient?

A.    Mr. Marusak's testimony primarily describes a broad routing methodology and regional
      environmental review process. The analysis relies heavily on GIS mapping and aerial
      photography rather than detailed property-specific investigations.

Q.    Did Mr. Marusak acknowledge that the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department
      recommended maximizing use of existing infrastructure corridors?

A.    Yes. Mr. Marusak testified that TPWD recommended using existing facilities wherever
      possible and paralleling existing utility and transportation corridors in order to minimize
      habitat fragmentation and environmental impacts.

Q.    Do you believe Link G9 follows those recommendations?

A.    No. Link G9 would create a new corridor directly through active ranchland and rural open
      space, rather than maximizing the use of existing, compatible infrastructure corridors
      where feasible. In my opinion, the proposed route would fragment agricultural land and
      wildlife habitat, including all of the Properties owned by SWG Briggs I, L.P. that are
      impacted by Link G9.

      A true and correct copy of a screenshot from Oncor's interactive map showing Link G9
      running through the properties owned by SWG Briggs I, L.P. was attached as Exhibit A to
      my Direct Testimony and is attached hereto as Exhibit A. As depicted in Exhibit A, County
      Road 218 runs east and west, and approximately halfway through Tract 5218, CR 218
      diverts south. No additional infrastructure runs through Tracts 5132 and 5133 (Properties
      owned by SWG Briggs I, L.P.). This does not demonstrate that Link G9 is making
      reasonable use of existing infrastructure.

Q.    Did Applicants acknowledge that landowners raised concerns regarding agriculture,
      property values, aesthetics, and health concerns?

A.    Yes. Mr. Marusak acknowledged that public comments included concerns regarding
      agricultural operations, property values, aesthetics, wildlife, and health effects. Those
      concerns directly apply to the Properties owned by SWG Briggs I, L.P. and surrounding
      community.

Q.    Do you believe Applicants adequately addressed those concerns?

A.    No. While Applicants acknowledged the concerns, they did not demonstrate that Link G9
      reasonably minimizes those impacts where feasible alternatives exist.




REBUTTAL TESTIMONY oF AMY G. THOMASON                                                              4
                         III.    REBUTTAL OF WELLS TESTIMONY

Q.    Have you reviewed the testimony of Kevin Wells?

A.    Yes.

Q.    What concerns do you have regarding Mr. Wells' testimony?

A.    Mr. Wells' assertion that all of the proposed routes minimize impacts to affected
      landowners and communities where feasible alternatives exist is inaccurate. In my opinion,
      this generalized assertion does not hold true.

Q.    Have you reviewed the routing requirements contained in 16 TAC § 25.101?

A.    Yes. The rules require that transmission lines be routed, "to the extent reasonable," to
      moderate impacts on affected landowners and communities. The rules also require
      consideration of whether routes utilize existing compatible corridors, parallel roads or
      property lines, and conform with prudent avoidance principles.

Q.    Do you believe Link G9 complies with those requirements?

A.    No. In my opinion, Link G9 does not adequately moderate impacts to affected landowners
      because it unnecessarily divides active ranchland and imposes severe and permanent
      impacts on agricultural operations, wildlife habitat, future residential use, aesthetics, and
      rural community values.

Q.    Do you believe Applicants sufficiently demonstrated that Link G9 is the least
      damaging reasonable alternative?

A.    No. Applicants have demonstrated that they conducted a routing study and developed
      multiple alternative routes; however, they have not shown that Link G9 appropriately
      minimizes impacts to the properties it traverses, including the Properties owned by SWG
      Briggs I, L.P., when compared to other feasible alternatives. In particular, Applicants have
      not demonstrated that Link G9 makes reasonable use of existing infrastructure corridors or
      otherwise avoids or reduces impacts to agricultural operations, rural land uses, and
      sensitive areas where such alternatives are available.

      As mentioned previously, and as depicted in Exhibit A, County Road 218 runs east and
      west, and approximately halfway through Tract 5218, CR 218 diverts south. No additional
      infrastructure runs through Tracts 5132 and 5133 (Properties owned by SWG Briggs I,
      L.P.). This does not demonstrate that Link G9 is making reasonable use of existing
      infrastructure.




REBUTTAL TESTIMONY oF AMY G. THOMASON                                                             5
 Q.    Do you believe Applicants provided adequate mitigation commitments specific to the
      Properties owned by SWG Briggs I, L.P.?

A.    No. Applicants primarily rely on generalized mitigation language such as impacts being
      minimized "where feasible" or "wherever possible. " These types of statements are
      inherently discretionary, vague, and unenforceable, and they do not provide meaningful or
      reliable protection against the substantial and permanent impacts associated with a 765 kV
      transmission corridor crossing the Properties.

      In my opinion, such generalized commitments fail to identify effective measures, defined
      standards, or enforceable limitations that would actually ensure impacts are avoided or
      reduced. As a result, they do not adequately address the long-term effects on agricultural
      operations, land use, wildlife habitat, or the overall character and functionality of the
      Properties.

Q.    As such, what do you request from the Commission?

A.    I respectfully request that the Commission reject Link G9 and all routes incorporating Link
      G9, including Routes 266,524,535,543,546,547,548,557,668,729,900, and 905. I
      further request that the Commission select routing alternatives that better utilize existing
      compatible infrastructure corridors and minimize impacts to agricultural operations, rural
      landowners, wildlife habitat, and the Northeast Burnet County Water District 1.

Q.    Does this conclude your rebuttal testimony?

A.    Yes, at present it does, but I reserve the right to amend or supplement my rebuttal testimony.
